summary: Independently verified the /wc fast-liveness policy with an isolated Node canary plus this worker's real launch beacon/pin/claim/heartbeat lineage. The durable test proves the 3m allocation-silent boundary, <6m active state, 6-10m stale-suspect window, >=10m retry-safe recovery eligibility, fresh-heartbeat precedence over old claim age, terminal blocking, deterministic G2 recovery with exactly one winner across five contenders, predecessor immutability/lineage, and loser re-entry. No product/current pointers were touched and this does not promote production /w.
evidence: local isolated execution of the exact committed canary source: PASS
tests: PASS: beacon <3m -> ALLOCATING; beacon at 3m without assignment -> ALLOCATION_SILENT.
PASS: latest signal <6m -> ACTIVE_OR_UNKNOWN; exactly 6m and just under 10m -> STALE_SUSPECT.
PASS: exactly 10m -> RECOVERY_ELIGIBLE only when retry-safe; unsafe retry remains blocked.
PASS: old claim plus fresh heartbeat -> ACTIVE_OR_UNKNOWN, so heartbeat freshness blocks time-only takeover.
PASS: 5 recovery contenders racing exact G000002 -> 1 winner / 4 losers; all observe the same winner.
PASS: G000001 predecessor bytes remain unchanged and G000002 carries predecessor lineage.
PASS: a recovery loser re-enters allocation on a different fixture job; terminal state creates no G000003.
unresolved: This verifies the binding policy and deterministic recovery primitive in isolated fixtures; it does not by itself prove every human-facing Live projection renders these states correctly.
Production /w remains outside this canary's authority and is not promoted by this result.
